title: Require newer version of Reactant

body:
Since #5586, `set_to_field!(::ReactantField, ::ReactantField)` takes the
CPU interpolation fallback whenever sizes or locations differ, including
for a reduced column field (e.g. a 1D reference profile) being set into
a full 3D field. Under Reactant tracing that fallback cannot work: its
first step, `on_architecture(CPU(), grid)`, rebuilds the traced grid
through the validating constructor, and validate_lat_lon_grid_args then
drives `||` with a `TracedRNumber{Bool}`:

    TypeError: non-boolean (Reactant.TracedRNumber{Bool}) used in boolean context

(and even past validation, traced data cannot be materialized on the CPU
mid-trace). Before #5586 this case was handled by the extension's plain
`interior(u) .= interior(v)` broadcast, which traces fine.

Restore that behavior by widening the fast path: a dimension may be
copied by broadcasting when both fields share its location and size, or
when v is reduced there (Nothing location, singleton size). The strict
old condition is a subset, so other cases are unchanged.

This fixes Breeze.jl's Reactant lat-lon compilation tests, broken since
its reference states became column fields set into 3D density fields
inside compiled functions (NumericalEarth/Breeze.jl#863).

---

Ref: https://github.com/NumericalEarth/Breeze.jl/pull/882#issuecomment-5152852279.
